title: First special sitting of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 50 members present. The Speaker announced the agenda and the chair sent the President's nominations for Deputy Chair of the Human Rights Commission, four ministers and two Anti-Corruption Commission members to committees. Members then debated the Independent Institutions Committee's reports on Broadcasting Commission and Elections Commission appointments; the Elections Commission debate quickly turned into a heated exchange, with many points of order, over claims that people were enrolled in the PNC without their knowledge. Members then voted: Uza. Aminath Saraahath Izzath and Mohamed Abdulla were approved for the Broadcasting Commission (Shifza Musthafa was not), and Mohamed Zahid and Abdul Rahman Salah Rasheed were approved for the Elections Commission. The sitting ended at 09:49 and the next sitting was set for 20 January 2025.

items.title: Votes on the nominees (Broadcasting Commission x3, Elections Commission x2)
items.outcome: Saraahath Izzath passed 68-0; Shifza Musthafa not passed 11-50; Mohamed Abdulla passed 58-2; Mohamed Zahid passed 68-0; Abdul Rahman Salah Rasheed passed 68-0

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said it is fitting for the public to hear how PNC members view the enrolment issue, quoting a PNC MP who called it shameful.
Asked why PNC membership forms were found inside the DNR and referred to a photo of the Home Minister there, which the minister has explained.
Said the Elections Commission should verify what happened and that the public is questioning the matter.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the Elections Commission is responsible for party registers and that the PNC's roughly 75,000 new members could include some added without their knowledge.
Argued that the MDP has also enrolled people into parties in the past, so this is not new.
Raised points of order objecting to how another member's remarks were handled.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the Independent Institutions Committee's reports on the Broadcasting Commission and Elections Commission nominees, saying candidates scoring 75% or more were listed.
Said both reports were passed by consensus of the committee members who attended.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Disputed a claim that members joined the PNC voluntarily, saying Hussain Ziyad was enrolled without any knowledge.
Said the Home Minister's name was being mentioned without cause and objected to claims being made.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Welcomed the committee's work during the recess and urged members to vote for honest, trustworthy people for these positions.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the Elections Commission itself had decided that a member's party form was not submitted by the member, and the chair should not criticise that decision.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said the PNC parliamentary group leader should not make claims about the MDP that cannot be proven, citing the President's remarks.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Raised a point of order saying the debate had drifted from the committee report and asked the chair to bring members back to the agenda.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Said accusations against the Home Minister were false and, if true, would be for a court to decide.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Said MDP-aligned members were repeatedly spreading falsehoods and noted that Hussain Ziyad has a history of switching parties.

decisions: Deputy Chair nomination for the Human Rights Commission referred to the Human Rights and Gender Committee.
Four ministerial nominations referred to the Committee on Government Accountability.
Two Anti-Corruption Commission nominations referred to the Independent Institutions Committee.
Uza. Aminath Saraahath Izzath approved as a Broadcasting Commission member (68-0).
Shifza Musthafa not approved as a Broadcasting Commission member (11-50).
Mohamed Abdulla approved as a Broadcasting Commission member (58-2).
Mohamed Zahid approved as an Elections Commission member (68-0).
Abdul Rahman Salah Rasheed approved as an Elections Commission member (68-0).
Next sitting set for 20 January 2025 at 09:00.
